newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB-Russia '96 net harvest seen 70 mln T.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-Russia '96 net harvest seen 70 mln T.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from the Agrokhleb Report, published by SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.
RUSSIAN 1996 NET GRAIN OUTPUT SEEN AT 70 MLN TONNES
MOSCOW, Nov 27 - Russia's 1996 net grain output will probably increase by 10 percent on last year's level to 70 million tonnes.
However, the harvest this year is still one of the lowest since 1960. Net output was lower only in 1963 (62.8 million tonnes), 1965 (66.3 million tonnes) and 1995 (63.4 million tonnes).
Provisional estimates are very close to SovEcon's forecasts produced in August, particularly for Siberia.
The collective farm sector accounted for the bulk of total output -- about 64 million tonnes out of the total 70 million.
Grain production increased in most regions, particularly in the Volga river basin (Povolzhsk and Volgo-Vyatsk regions) and in the Urals.
However, output in all regions is below the 1991-95 average.
In addition, grain output in Western Siberia, Eastern Siberia and the Northern Caucasus declined on last year.

In the Northern Caucasus, grain output is particularly low -- about seven million tonnes below the 1991-95 average. As a result, grain deliveries from this region, which usually leads the list of domestic grain suppliers, will drop in 1996/97.
